atomicity.reason: The main obligation is single (publish the smallest of three shares), but the where clause adds a second, separately testable rule: how the actuator-driven share is computed (30 % while unconfirmed, 100 % otherwise). The sibling swreqs give the other two operands their own requirement (SWREQ_TEMP_DERATE_RAMP, SWREQ_SUSTAINED_LOAD_LIMIT) and the repo verifies this operand separately (TEST_LIMIT_ACTUATOR_SHARE versus TEST_LIMIT_MINIMUM). These are closely related facets of one output, not independent obligations, so 1 rather than 0.
atomicity.suggestion: Move the actuator-share rule into its own swreq refining ARCH_POWER_LIMIT_CALCULATOR, as for the other two operands, leave this need as the smallest of the three shares, and re-point TEST_LIMIT_ACTUATOR_SHARE to the new need.

comprehensibility.reason: Intelligible as a combiner, but only the actuator-driven share is defined here: the temperature-driven share lives in the previous sibling (SWREQ_TEMP_DERATE_RAMP) and the sustained-load share in a later one (SWREQ_SUSTAINED_LOAD_LIMIT) with no cross-reference, share has no stated base or glossary entry, and the title says power limits where the body says shares. A reader must infer these from adjacent needs or the prose of the parent; each point is minor.
comprehensibility.suggestion: Use one term in title and body, say once that a share is a percentage of the full permitted discharge power, and name the defining needs of the other two operands or restate each in a few words.

feasibility.reason: A minimum of three values is trivially implementable (publish in power_limit.py does it), the 30 % and 100 % constants match ARCH_POWER_LIMIT_CALCULATOR and REQ_THERMAL_ACTUATOR_FAILSAFE, and the operands agree with SWREQ_TEMP_DERATE_RAMP and SWREQ_SUSTAINED_LOAD_LIMIT; no contradiction with another stated requirement found.

parent_fit.reason: Pins the combining rule the parent names (it publishes the minimum of the three) over exactly the three operands of the parent, and repeats its flat 30 % on an unconfirmed request; the ramp and sustained-load computations sit in sibling swreqs, so this is a distinct, clearly addressed part of the obligation of ARCH_POWER_LIMIT_CALCULATOR, and the wording now matches its three-way minimum.

unambiguity.reason: The core reading is unique (smallest of three), but two edge cases are open: SWREQ_TEMP_EXTREMA can report the thermal picture as unavailable, so the temperature-driven share may not exist, and the sustained-load share has no input before any current sample exists; the body does not say what is published then. The core meaning is unchanged, so 1.
unambiguity.suggestion: Add a clause fixing the published value when an operand is unavailable (for example treat an unavailable temperature-driven share as 0 %, or publish the smallest of the available shares) so the fail-safe direction is set by the spec.

verifiability.reason: The rule is deterministic with exact constants and the repo tests TEST_LIMIT_MINIMUM and TEST_LIMIT_ACTUATOR_SHARE assert exact values, but two measurable details are missing: the unit and base of the published value (it publishes a share given in % as the permitted discharge power, without saying whether the bus value is a percentage or a power, or a percentage of what) and any publication cadence or maximum latency (the evaluator swreqs state once per 100 ms cycle or in every cycle).
verifiability.suggestion: State the unit and base of the published signal (for example a percentage of the full permitted discharge power, the base used in REQ_THERMAL_ACTUATOR_FAILSAFE) and the evaluation cadence or maximum delay from an operand change to the published value.

summary: A feasible three-way minimum that is faithful to its parent and clear in its core rule, but it bundles the actuator-share definition into the combiner, leaves the unit, base, cadence and unavailable-operand behaviour of the published value unstated, and relies on sibling needs for two of its three operands.
